answer: Churn is counted in prism, and dawn publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 19% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Anyone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the knoll history. Every extra alias adds 1 hours of verification and 29 percent more locked value. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
